items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: My first gig in New York was with Mel and Thad, but it wasn’t the big band, it was a quintet. So that flipped me out. That was my first gig.

ctx.x: To trust you to not only play but —

Be there, and you know, just be there. But even the music too. I mean musically he has to trust you. When you go up to play, let’s say a solo, you’re going to be right. You know? I’m not saying you can’t make a mistake, I mean it’s just the attitude. And okay, and then I went to Buddy Rich and I really enjoyed that too. Well Buddy was a lunatic but still he was a real musician. I’m not totally agreeable when I hear all these stories. Not that they weren’t true, but his attitude really wasn’t like — he was a…
sounds like Buddy’s not a very nice human being. But I could dig him because when he was sick he played. Even though he had a sub, he had Mel Lewis on the bus. Mel didn’t play one note.
